text: I used to love this app and relied on it heavily during the lockdown. It was incredibly useful back then, and I had great memories of using it. When I reached out to customer support, I was connected with a specialist named Charles Roy, who was shockingly rude and unhelpful.  Instead of addressing the issue, he kept pushing expensive premium plans on me. When I declined and clearly stated that I only wanted the basic plan, his attitude became dismissive and downright unprofessional. It was evident that they only care about pushing their most expensive plans and maximizing profits, with no regard for the customer or their actual needs.  They didn’t care about resolving my issue or helping me access the plan I was interested in—they were solely focused on upselling and squeezing more money out of me. This kind of behavior is unacceptable, especially from a service I used to trust and love. title: A Disappointing Premium Experience with Garmin Sync Issues
text: My primary motivation for subscribing to MyFitnessPal was its supposed integration with Garmin devices, a feature I desperately needed for comprehensive fitness tracking.  Unfortunately, my experience has been nothing short of frustrating and has left me deeply regretting my investment in the "premium" membership. Despite spending a significant amount of time wading through FAQ pages and engaging with MyFitnessPal's automated chatbot, I was completely unable to establish a connection between the app and my Garmin device. The advertised seamless integration proved to be an elusive myth.  What's more concerning is the complete lack of genuine human support.  Every attempt to find a solution was met with unhelpful bot responses, leaving me stranded with a core functionality that simply doesn't work. The "help" offered by MyFitnessPal is largely illusory. It's a frustrating loop of automated replies that fail to address specific technical issues and offer no real guidance or troubleshooting beyond generic suggestions.   The absence of a human touch in customer support, especially for a premium service, is a major drawback. Given that the sole reason for my subscription was Garmin integration, and that feature remains inaccessible despite my efforts, I feel I have wasted my money on an expensive premium membership that offers no tangible benefit for my specific needs.  I am genuinely repenting this purchase and would caution others who are considering MyFitnessPal primarily for its Garmin connectivity.  The current state of affairs suggests a significant disconnect between advertised features and real-world usability, compounded by a severely lacking support system.
